The US government cannot afford higher interest rates.

If interest rates average +150 basis points above CBO’s February projections by 2036, US deficits would increase by nearly $6 trillion over this period.

The deficit would then rise to 8.8% of GDP, the highest level since WWII, excluding 2008 and 2020.

This would also push the US public Debt-to-GDP ratio to a record 133%, up from ~100% currently.

If rates average +50 basis points above projections, deficits would increase by nearly $2 trillion, lifting the Debt-to-GDP ratio to 124% by 2036.

Just weeks ago, the 10Y Note yield traded at ~5.30%, or ~100 basis points above CBO’s average projected rate over the next 10 years.

The US government needs rate cuts.

With bond yields coming off the boil last week, perhaps we are now settling into a range for a bit. While the CPI came in hotter than expected, there is currently little pressure on the Fed to raise rates at the end of October. While the consensus appears to be that yields have moved higher because of strong economic growth, and that they are now moving a bit lower because of a possible slowdown in AI capex, in my view the rise in yields this year has been multi-factorial, including sticky structural inflation and mounting fiscal risk.

If the earnings boom continues, the CAPE ratio will likely come down as the newer higher estimates come in and the older lower numbers roll off.

BREAKING: China purchased +25 tonnes of gold in August via the London OTC market, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.

This is +25% more than the official +20 tonnes reported by China's central bank for this month.

This also follows estimated purchases of +35, +40, and +48 tonnes in July, June, and May, respectively.

Over these 4 months, China's estimated gold purchases through the OTC market exceeded officially reported purchases by 83 tonnes, or +128%.

Meanwhile, global central banks are estimated to have acquired +79 tonnes of gold in August, +365% above the pre-2022 average of +17 tonnes.

China is stockpiling gold.

US energy stocks are having a historic year:

The S&P 500 Equal Weight Energy ETF, $RSPG, is up +49.2% YTD, trading near its all-time high.

$RSPG covers US energy sector stocks in the S&P 500, with each company receiving an approximately equal weight.

The fund is now on track for its 3rd-strongest annual return since its inception in 2006.

This would also mark its 6th consecutive annual gain, its longest winning streak on record.

Only two years have had higher returns, in 2021 and 2022, at +53.7% and +52.2%, respectively.

Over the last 2 weeks, $RSPG has risen +7.5%, and if that pace continues, the fund could record its strongest annual return since inception.

Energy stocks are thriving amid the Iran War.

🗳️ Libby sees wave conditions forming. Trump's net approval is about 20 points underwater, the generic ballot sits near D+9, and Democrats hold the enthusiasm edge. Republicans have just a three-seat House majority to defend.

🏛️ The Senate is harder. Democrats need to hold Michigan, Georgia, and New Hampshire and flip four more in states like Ohio, Iowa, North Carolina, Maine, Alaska, and Texas. Kalshi, Nate Silver, and Split Ticket put Democratic odds at roughly 63% to 70%.

🏗️ About 70% of voters now disapprove of data centers, up from roughly even in September 2025. The backlash is bipartisan, and Libby expects moratoriums, tougher permitting, and higher costs for the AI build-out in 2027 and beyond.

📊 Libby expects risk assets to prefer a split Congress over a Democratic sweep. Deficits likely rise either way, with Democrats possibly trading defense spending for ACA subsidies and reversed Medicaid cuts, a mix that could push yields higher.

🏦 A Democratic Senate would likely block controversial Fed nominees, and Chair Warsh is still just one of 12 votes on the FOMC.

BREAKING: The Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -300,000 barrels last week, to 282.7 million barrels, the lowest level since October 1982.

Since March 20th, US oil inventories in the SPR have dropped -132.8 million, or -32%.

We have now seen drawdowns in 29 of the last 30 weeks.

For perspective, oil reserves in the SPR stood at 653.9 million barrels in 2020, or +131% above current levels.

Meanwhile, commercial crude oil stocks excluding the SPR dropped -3.1 million barrels last week, to 412.5 million barrels, the lowest reading since the end of July.

This is also ~3% below the 5-year average for this time of year.

America's oil stockpiles are at critically low levels.
